title: The Omen
logline: Ted runs into the same stranger nine times in sixteen days and builds a fate map that spirals toward a Thursday cab stand, only to learn that the woman in the mustard cardigan lives across the street, has seen the map through his window, and is an actuary with a chart proving Ted is her bad-luck omen. Meanwhile Barney tries to schedule fate across fourteen Manhattan hotspots and becomes the guardian angel of one gutter salesman from Dayton, and Lily's oldest secret about how she met Marshall finally slips out.
coldOpen: Kids, in the fall of 2013, I ran into the same woman nine times in sixteen days. I was sure the universe was trying to tell me something. So was she.

couch.line: She is not your mother. She did, however, think I was a curse.

guests.name: Wren Talbot
guests.role: an insurance actuary and weekend birder who prices risk for a living, believes in exactly one irrational thing, and has charted proof that the man across the street is her bad-luck omen; brisk, precise and dry, always in a mustard cardigan

guests.name: Lonnie Haskins
guests.role: a cheerful gutter salesman from Dayton, Ohio, on his first trip to New York, following a guidebook itinerary to the minute; keeps running into Barney everywhere and decides Barney is his guardian angel

scenes.summary: Tuesday morning on the 6 train. Ted waits for sighting number nine; Robin says people get on trains. The woman in the mustard cardigan boards, Marshall waves at fate, she says 'oh no', Ted hears 'oh, you'. She gets off one stop later. Ted has data. And a map. There's string.

beats.line: Tuesday morning, the downtown 6 train. Sighting number nine was due at Fifty-First Street.
Ted, you're staring at that door like it owes you money.
Fifty-First Street. She gets on at Fifty-First two Tuesdays out of three.
The cardigan woman, Robin. Ted's seen her eight times in two weeks.
People get on trains, Marshall. That's kind of the whole idea of trains.
Eight times. The subway. The grocery store. The cab line. My dentist.
His dentist, Robin!
So she lives nearby and she has teeth.
Ted. Mustard cardigan. Two o'clock.
Okay. Everybody act natural.
Marshall! Don't wave at fate!
Oh no.
Did you hear that? She said, oh, you. Like, oh, you again. My favorite stranger.
She said, oh no.
Actually, oh you and oh no share a diphthong.
So does go away.
She's getting off! She got on one stop ago! Who rides one stop?
Someone fleeing.
Or someone shy. Fate makes people shy, Robin.
Fate is making her walk eleven blocks in heels.
Ted has data, Robin. He has a map.
Of course there's a map.
Tonight. MacLaren's. Eight o'clock. Bring an open mind.
There's string.

scenes.summary: Ted presents the fate map: nine pins, a golden spiral, a prediction for Thursday at 6:15 at a cab stand on 23rd and Park. Robin notes every pin is within four blocks of his apartment. Marshall cites fate: the housing office put Lily three doors down. Lily whispers to Robin that she paid a girl named Denise forty dollars to switch rooms. Barney arrives and sees marketing: he'll hit Manhattan's fourteen hottest spots so every woman sees him three times, then close with 'We have to stop meeting like this.' Robin bets twenty no woman calls it fate. Button: fate's a slow talker.

beats.line: That night, I presented my findings. I had prepared remarks.
Ted, you brought a corkboard to a bar.
It's not a corkboard, Lily. It's a fate map.
It's a corkboard.
Connect the pins, and you get a perfect golden spiral. The shape of seashells. And galaxies.
beats.title: The Fate Map: Findings
lines: Subway 4, grocery 2, cab line 2, my dentist 1
Connect the pins: a golden spiral

beats.line: I did the string.
Ted, every pin on that board is within four blocks of your apartment.
Four and a half.
What's her name?
I don't know her name. On the map, she's the Woman in the Mustard Cardigan. Mustard, for short.
You named your soulmate after a condiment.
Dijon, technically. It's a warmer yellow.
Ted, have you said one single word to her?
Words would ruin it. Right now she could be anyone. A poet. A cellist. A woman who restores antique maps.
A woman who keeps seeing the same guy at her dentist.
Robin, fate is how I met Lily. Out of four thousand students, Wesleyan put the most beautiful girl three doors down from me.
That's not luck. That's the universe with a clipboard.
Mm-hm. The universe. Clipboard.
I paid a girl named Denise forty dollars to switch rooms.
Nineteen years, and you never told him?
It's the only secret I've ever kept. I have no idea how I'm doing it.
What are you two whispering about?
Fate! How real it is! How nobody paid for it!
Why is there a corkboard in my bar? Did somebody lose a cat?
Ted keeps running into the same beautiful stranger all over the city. Nine times. He thinks it's fate.
Ted. Do you realize what you've discovered?
Love?
Marketing.
A guy hits on a woman, she says no. The same guy shows up three times by coincidence? She thinks it's destiny.
Women don't want a man. They want a sign. And Daddy is about to become a billboard.
Barney, you can't manufacture fate. That's the entire point of fate.
Please. Fate is just a schedule somebody else made.
Tomorrow, I hit the fourteen hottest spots in Manhattan at peak hours. Ranjit drives. Every woman in this city sees me three times.
And then I close. We have to stop meeting like this.
Barney, I've seen you every day since 2005. I've been trying to stop meeting like this for years.
A woman sees the same guy in a suit fourteen times, she doesn't think fate. She thinks pepper spray.
Not if it's a really good suit.
Twenty bucks says not one woman calls it fate.
Challenge accepted. It was written.
So Thursday at six fifteen, at the center of your spiral, you'll finally talk to her?
Thursday at six fifteen, I'll let fate finish its sentence.
Ted, it's been sixteen days. Fate's a slow talker.

scenes.summary: Thursday, 6:15, pouring rain, one cab. Ted and Marshall, his witness, are in it when the woman in the mustard cardigan climbs in to share. She's Wren Talbot, she lives across the street, she's seen the fern, the robe and the corkboard. The cab stand is outside her office; the spiral is her commute. Every time she sees Ted, something goes wrong within the hour, and she has a chart. Ted tries the line; she changed dry cleaners to avoid him. She has a meteorologist boyfriend. The cab gets a flat. 'Seventeen.' She walks. Button: tomorrow at seven, she'll see the robe.

beats.line: Thursday, six fifteen, the center of the spiral. It was pouring, there was one cab, and Marshall came as my witness.
Six fourteen, Ted. One minute to destiny. I brought granola bars in case destiny runs late.
She'll be here, Marshall. The spiral doesn't lie.
Sorry, it's pouring. Do you mind if I share?
Oh no.
Ten.
Hi. Ted Mosby. Architect.
I know.
You know?
Wren Talbot. I live across the street from you. Fourth floor.
Every morning at seven, you water a fern in a very short bathrobe.
Dad. How short?
A perfectly respectable length, Luke. Mid-thigh. Upper mid-thigh.
Ted. She's seen the robe.
How long have you lived across the street?
Two years. Your fern and I are very close.
Wren, this is going to sound crazy, but I have a map.
The corkboard with the spiral? Ted, it faces the window.
You can read it from across the street?
I'm a birder. My name is Wren. It was always going to happen.
Also, the center of your spiral is the cab stand outside my office. I'm there every day at six fifteen.
Every day?
For six years.
Buddy. The spiral is her commute.
Okay. But every time you see me, you say, oh no. Why?
Because you're my omen.
I'm an actuary. I price risk for an insurance company. So I tracked you.
Every time I see you, something goes wrong within the hour. Sixteen for sixteen.
beats.title: Within One Hour of Seeing Ted

beats.line: Sixteen? I've only seen you nine times.
You've noticed me nine times.
What's the pigeon incident?
Twice. Same pigeon. It was personal.
Wren, correlation isn't causation!
Ted, I teach a seminar on that. Everyone's allowed one irrational thing. Mine is you.
That's funny. I think mine is you.
Say the line, Ted. Say the line.
Well. We have to stop meeting like this.
Yes! That's my whole plan! I changed dry cleaners because of you.
The one on Second Avenue? I switched to that one last week!
I know. You were there.
Wren, one dinner. A controlled experiment. If nothing bad happens, I'm not an omen.
That's sweet, Ted. But I have a boyfriend. He's a meteorologist.
Oh. Is it serious?
Sixty percent chance of forever.
Guys? The driver says we have a flat tire. He says he's never had a flat tire.
Seventeen.
I'll walk. Statistically, it's safer.
She'll be in her window tomorrow morning. At seven.
And you'll be in the robe.
Oh no.

scenes.summary: Friday night. Robin was right: nearby. Barney returns from fourteen stops: no women called it fate, but one man saw him at every one. Montage of Lonnie from Dayton everywhere. Robin: it's a bus tour. Lonnie arrives via Ranjit, says the line, and turns out to have found his nerve in Barney's suit; Barney is touched, and booked for the Statue of Liberty. Barney sells out Lily, Robin took fifty, and Lily's forty-dollar room swap comes out in a Wesleyan flashback. Marshall: most romantic thing anyone's ever paid for. Ted, at the window: Lily knew; he made a map because he didn't. Nobody could live in a city made of cathedrals. Wren holds up a sign across the street: eighteen. Risotto.

beats.line: Across the street. I said nearby. I want it on the record that I said nearby.
Ted, a woman made a chart about you. That's more effort than anyone you've ever dated.
She's an actuary, Lily. For an actuary, a chart is basically a mixtape.
Fourteen locations. Nine hours. Ranjit cried twice. Once in a tunnel.
So. How many women called it fate?
Zero women. But one man saw me at all fourteen stops.
Morning, neighbor! Big city, huh?
Hey, you again! What are the odds?
We have to stop meeting like this!
Your driver let me in! Nice fella!
Lonnie. From Dayton. He sells gutters. He thinks I'm his guardian angel.
Dayton's lovely.
Barney, you hit the fourteen most famous spots in Manhattan at rush hour. That's not a fate schedule. That's a bus tour.
Barney! Ranjit gave me your address! Nice fella!
Ranjit.
That's fifteen! We have to stop meeting like this!
We really, really do.
I came here to decide if I should start my own gutter business. And everywhere I went, there was your suit.
It never said a word. But I heard it. Go for it, Lonnie.
It does say that.
Lonnie, lots of people have seen me three times in one day. You're the first one who was happy about it.
Statue of Liberty tomorrow? Nine a.m.?
Eight forty-five. Beat the crowds.
Fine. I owe you twenty. But at least I'm not the only one who manufactured fate. Right, Lily?
Robin!
He offered me fifty.
Manufactured what?
Nothing! Fate! Forty dollars! Denise!
Move-in day. I saw a boy carry a futon up four flights by himself, singing. I needed to be on that hallway.
Hi! I'm Lily. I just moved in three doors down. Totally at random.
Whoa. Out of four thousand students? What are the odds?
Forty dollars.
Didn't she live in the other building an hour ago?
Ted. Don't question a miracle.
You bought the hallway?
I bought the hallway, Marshmallow. Everything after that was you.
Forty dollars?
And my good lamp. Denise drove a hard bargain.
Lilypad. That is the most romantic thing anyone has ever paid for.
I'd have gone for a hundred.
Lily paid forty dollars because she knew. I built a whole map because I didn't.
Ted, maybe she's not a sign. Maybe she's just a nice part of your Tuesday.
I want every coincidence to be a cathedral. But most of a city is small stuff. Doorknobs. Windowsills.
A neighbor who thinks you broke her heel.
Nobody could live in a city made of cathedrals.
Marshall, are you crying?
I just found out I was purchased, Lily. It's a big night.
She's in her window. She's holding up a sign. It says eighteen.
And underneath, it just says, risotto.
Kids, Wren and I waved every morning for four more years. We never had that dinner. It was plenty.
And in her spreadsheet, the day I met your mother is logged as: stepped in gum.
